notes: Two nodes built against different versions of moveit_msgs/DisplayTrajectory; generated message definitions diverged so the md5sum (interface definition hash) differs. Same msg_type name on both ends, but the Sig definition-hash mismatch causes silent subscription failure. Encoded as identical msg_type (name matches) on a PAIR edge; the catch comes from Sig def-hash equality, which a checker derives from the message-definition content rather than the type name. Gold = Sig (def hash) + Ver (the divergence arose across versions).

roscpp publisher vs rosjava subscriber generated divergent definitions for the same custom message, producing an md5 mismatch. Type name matches across the edge; the failure is a Sig definition-hash divergence between two independently generated client-library codecs. Encoded same msg_type both sides; checker catch is on the def-hash, plus Ver because the generated defs drifted.

Pub/sub message-format mismatch: the interface type was assumed but not declared, so publisher and subscriber bound to the same topic with incompatible message types. Encoded as a genuine type mismatch on the edge (std_msgs/String vs std_msgs/Int32) since the bug IS a Sig type incompatibility. Representative types chosen; the corpus does not name the exact pair, but the mechanism is type-on-type incompatibility caught by Sig.
excluded: modeled from failure taxonomy (Canelas et al. 2024), not a documented bug instance

notes: Canonical ECM-Sig.frame case from PhysFrame: sensor data published in the sensor's own frame is consumed as if in base_link, corrupting geometry. Same msg_type; the bug is a frame mismatch (producer frame=base_scan, consumer expects base_link). Frame is the implicit contract PhysFrame type-checks. Units identical (m); only the frame field differs to encode the documented inconsistency.
excluded: constructed/illustrative archetype of the PhysFrame frame-mismatch class (Kate et al. 2021), not a specific documented instance; PhysFrame reports the class statistically (190 instances across 180 projects) but does not catalogue this node pair. Flagged by independent reconstruction and excluded for consistency with the modeled-case screening bar.

notes: Unit-convention mismatch on geometry_msgs/Twist: producer emits values in cm (or otherwise non-REP-103 units) while consumer expects REP-103 SI (m/s). REP-103 mandates m, m/s, rad, rad/s. The semantic unit is an unwritten convention not encoded in the .msg type, so the type matches but the units field differs. Encoded units cm (producer) vs m_s (consumer); same msg_type and frame. Catch = Sig.units.
excluded: source is a usage question about radian units, not a documented defect (verified via source)

notes: Semantic-type mismatch where the .msg type matches but the meaning differs: RGB published, BGR expected (or deg vs rad on an angle field). The wire type (sensor_msgs/Image) is identical on both ends, so a pure type check passes. The catch is only PARTIAL and only possible if Sig carries a semantic-encoding annotation beyond the .msg type. Encoded same msg_type/frame; the semantic distinction (RGB vs BGR) is documented in notes since the canonical token set has no color-encoding field. units=none (no SI unit applies to an image color encoding).
excluded: modeled from failure taxonomy (Canelas et al. 2024), not a documented bug instance

notes: Namespace/remapping typo yields a silent no-connection: the role/type both match in the contract, but the actual topic-name binding (an implicit wiring detail) was mis-remapped so no edge ever forms. Sig declares the role correctly, but a wiring typo can slip past a contract that only checks declared role+type. PARTIAL catch. Encoded as a matching PAIR (type/frame/units all agree) because the contract surfaces are compatible; the failure is in the runtime name binding, not the declared contract.
excluded: modeled from failure taxonomy (Canelas et al. 2024), not a documented bug instance

notes: Strongest Beh case: BEST_EFFORT publisher vs RELIABLE subscriber. Per the DDS QoS compatibility matrix (design.ros2.org/articles/qos.html), a RELIABLE reader requesting from a BEST_EFFORT writer is an incompatible request and no messages flow. Encoded producer.qos.reliability=best_effort, consumer.qos.reliability=reliable, same msg_type. Catch = Beh.QoS.reliability.

rosbridge subscriber defaults to RELIABLE and silently fails to subscribe to a BEST_EFFORT publisher (e.g. a camera stream). Same QoS-reliability incompatibility as B-Beh-01 (best_effort producer vs reliable consumer). Same msg_type both ends; only qos.reliability differs. Catch = Beh.QoS.reliability.

Incompatible QoS with no warning on ROS 2 Foxy: a reliability mismatch (best_effort vs reliable) prevented delivery and the middleware gave no diagnostic. Encoded as best_effort producer vs reliable consumer, identical msg_type. Catch = Beh.QoS.reliability (the static contract surfaces this even though Foxy's runtime did not warn).

Durability contract mismatch on /map: map_server latches the map with TRANSIENT_LOCAL so late joiners get the last map, but a VOLATILE subscriber that joins after publication misses it entirely. Encoded producer.qos.durability=transient_local vs consumer.qos.durability=volatile, same msg_type/frame. The corpus describes the failure as a VOLATILE subscriber missing a TRANSIENT_LOCAL latched map. Catch = Beh.QoS.durability. (Note: a volatile request from a transient_local offer is technically DDS-compatible, but the documented operational failure is the late subscriber missing the latched sample; encoded faithfully to the documented durability disagreement.)

tf2 ExtrapolationException stalls nav: timestamps are unsynchronized (often a use_sim_time mismatch between nodes). The contract can catch a STATIC use_sim_time / clock-source disagreement, but not runtime timestamp drift. PARTIAL catch. Encoded as a tf PAIR with matching declared contract; the documented mismatch is a configuration/timing assumption (use_sim_time) that the canonical token set does not have a field for, so it is captured in notes. frame=per_message (TF carries frames per transform). Gold straddles Beh (timing assumption) and Rec (staleness).
excluded: source closed by maintainer as user configuration error (missing use_sim_time), not a project defect (verified)

notes: Timeliness failure: consumer expects 30 Hz for stable control but producer delivers only 5 Hz, yielding stale control. The refresh rate is an unstated assumption. Encoded producer.rate_hz=5 vs consumer.min_rate_hz=30, same msg_type/units. Catch = Beh.refresh_rate (rate_hz < min_rate_hz is a clean static contract violation). Representative msg_type (JointState feedback) chosen; corpus cites Ref [4] Timeliness category generically.
excluded: modeled from failure taxonomy (Canelas et al. 2024), not a documented bug instance

notes: nav2 keeps publishing motion after a goal cancel: the post-cancel state (robot should stop) is not honored. This is a behavioral postcondition / recovery-semantics failure that a STATIC composition check only partially predicts; it needs a behavioral/runtime test. PARTIAL catch. Encoded as a matching cmd_vel PAIR (contract surfaces agree) because the bug is a postcondition violation, not a surface incompatibility; documented in notes. Overlaps B-Rec-02. Also cited arXiv:2507.10235.

Deadline/liveliness QoS mismatch prevents connection: per the DDS QoS request-vs-offered rules, a reader requesting a tighter deadline (50 ms) than the writer offers (100 ms) is incompatible and no connection forms. Encoded producer deadline_ms=100 vs consumer deadline_ms=50, same msg_type. Catch = Beh.QoS.deadline. (Liveliness is the analogous case but the canonical qos schema only exposes deadline_ms; encoded via the deadline field.)
excluded: sourced from a design document (QoS request-vs-offered rules), describes a mechanism not a documented bug instance

notes: Canonical ECM-Res case: two independent modules both publish to /cmd_vel with no single owner, causing erratic motion (the documented fix is twist_mux to arbitrate). Modeled as a CONCURRENT exclusive-resource conflict: both producer.exclusive and consumer.exclusive declare the token actuation:/cmd_vel, so the checker flags a double-claim on an exclusive actuation resource. Catch = Res.exclusive_lock.
excluded: source is an architectural how-to question, not a documented defect (verified)

notes: ros2_control 'command interface already claimed' error on controller switch: two controllers both require an exclusive hardware command interface. Modeled CONCURRENT with both sides claiming the exclusive token hw_interface:joint1/position. No pub/sub edge (controllers claim interfaces, not topics), so outputs/inputs are empty. Catch = Res.exclusive_lock (double-claim of a command interface).

switch_controller returns OK despite a resource conflict: the exclusive claim collides but the failure is silent (the API reports success). Same exclusive-claim structure as B-Res-02, both sides claim hw_interface:joint1/position. The notable feature is silent failure, so the static contract is MORE predictive than the runtime API. Catch = Res.exclusive_lock.

Multiple Franka arms: interfaces wrongly reported as claimed due to ownership-bookkeeping errors across arms. Modeled as a static double-claim of an exclusive hardware interface (hw_interface:fr3_joint1/effort) by two controllers. Catch is PARTIAL ('Yes partly') because the static double-claim is detectable but the deeper per-arm bookkeeping is runtime. Catch = Res.exclusive_lock (partial). [independent-reconstruction correction: real interfaces are DISJOINT (panda_1 vs panda_3 effort); the bug is an unscoped implementation check, not an interface-level resource conflict. Re-encoded honestly -> checker correctly does not fire -> Res miss.]

Cannot activate multiple chainable controllers: a chained-interface availability conflict that surfaced post-upgrade. Modeled CONCURRENT on a shared chainable-interface exclusive token (chainable_interface:controllerA/reference). Gold = Res (interface availability conflict) + Ver (regression appeared after an upgrade; see also B-Ver-03 which encodes the version delta). Catch = Res + Ver.
excluded: duplicate of B-Ver-03 (same ros2_control#1400 defect; both gold {Res,Ver}); kept as a single multi-label case to avoid double-counting one underlying bug

notes: Two robots' nav stacks conflict because they share global (un-namespaced) topics: each robot implicitly assumes exclusive single-robot ownership of /cmd_vel (and other shared topics). Modeled CONCURRENT with both robots claiming actuation:/cmd_vel. Gold = Res (implicit exclusive single-robot ownership) + Sig (the real fix is namespace separation, a name-binding issue). Catch = Res + Sig namespace.
excluded: source is labelled a usage question, not a documented defect (verified)

notes: Embedded-DSL stack needs a localization update rate/bandwidth that the upstream module does not provide: a resource (rate/bandwidth) requirement that was left unstated. Modeled as a PAIR with a rate shortfall (producer rate_hz=10 vs consumer min_rate_hz=50) on the localization odometry edge, which is the most contract-expressible form of an unmet rate/bandwidth resource requirement. Representative rates chosen; corpus cites Ref [4] Embedded-DSL generically. Catch = Res (resource-rate requirement).
excluded: modeled from failure taxonomy (Canelas et al. 2024), not a documented bug instance

notes: SROS2 enclave access-control policy does not authorize a composed module's topic, so communication is denied (or, in a misconfig, wrongly permitted). [UNVERIFIED] as a real field incident; the mechanism (SROS2 policy XML) exists but no GitHub-issue-grade composition failure was found. Modeled as a PAIR where the consumer's perm_requires (sros2:publish:/composed_module/topic) is not granted by the producing/composing module's permission grant set, so a permission-boundary check would flag the unauthorized topic. Catch = Perm (config-consistency, not a field failure).
excluded: self-flagged UNVERIFIED: no documented composition-failure instance (SROS2 access-control mechanism only)

notes: A controller composed without a speed-restricted-zone constraint emits unsafe velocity near humans (ISO 10218 / TS 15066 speed-and-separation envelope). [UNVERIFIED] as a real incident; nav2 #1455 is a feature request, not a bug. Modeled as the velocity-producing module requiring (perm_requires) the safety_zone:speed_restricted:<=0.25m_s permission/envelope that the composition does not enforce, so its emitted m/s exceeds the zone limit. PARTIAL catch (Perm envelope vs zone limit). Velocity limit value (0.25 m/s) is illustrative of a TS 15066 reduced-speed envelope, not a documented number.
excluded: self-flagged UNVERIFIED: cited nav2#1455 is a feature request, not a bug

notes: nav2 recovery oscillation: the local recovery (spin/backup) and a downstream retreat behavior issue conflicting motion commands, and the arbitration between recovery strategies is a runtime decision. Rec declares the recovery strategy, but the arbitration is runtime, so a static check is PARTIAL. Modeled as a CONCURRENT conflict over a recovery-arbitration exclusive token on /cmd_vel (two recovery behaviors both driving the base). Also cited answers.ros.org/question/399916. Catch = Rec (partial; strategy declared, arbitration runtime).
excluded: sourced from project documentation (nav2 behavior trees), describes a mechanism not a documented bug instance

notes: 'Continues moving when cancel' — the abort/cancel postcondition (robot halts) is not honored. This is a recovery-semantics / behavioral-postcondition failure that needs a behavioral test; a static composition check is PARTIAL. Overlaps B-Beh-07 (same underlying nav2 cancel behavior). Modeled as a matching cmd_vel PAIR because the surfaces agree; the failure is a postcondition violation captured in notes. Gold = Rec (abort postcondition) + Beh.

Stale data after a sensor dropout, with no staleness-recovery contract: the consumer keeps using old data because there is no declared staleness timeout / recovery behavior. PARTIAL catch (a Rec/Beh staleness-timeout field would catch it; the canonical qos schema has no staleness-timeout field, so encoded via the rate expectation and documented in notes). Modeled as a sensor PAIR with a declared min_rate_hz=10 expectation; the dropout (rate falling to 0) and absent recovery contract are the documented mechanism. Gold = Rec (staleness recovery) + Beh.
excluded: modeled from failure taxonomy (Canelas et al. 2024), not a documented bug instance

notes: Strongest Ver case: a message definition changed across package versions, so the md5sum (interface hash) changed and a subscriber built against the old definition can no longer subscribe. Modeled as UPGRADE: interface_hash_old != interface_hash_new, semver 1.0.0 -> 2.0.0, changed_fields lists the definition edit. The changed field set intersects the consumer's reads (header), so it is a breaking change. Also cites /10628. Gold = Ver (hash skew) + Sig (the definition itself). Hashes/semver illustrative of the documented md5 change.

franka_msgs md5 error after a version change: FrankaState definition changed between franka_ros releases, producing an md5 mismatch so the consumer cannot subscribe. Modeled UPGRADE with hash skew old!=new and a changed FrankaState definition. consumer_reads include fields likely touched (robot_state/q/dq). Gold = Ver + Sig. Hashes/semver illustrative; the documented fact is the post-version-change md5 error.

ros2_control chainable controllers broke after a framework upgrade: the chainable-interface contract changed across versions, breaking activation. Modeled UPGRADE with a framework-API hash change (chainable_v1 -> chainable_v2) and changed chainable-interface semantics. Same underlying issue as B-Res-05 (encoded there as the resource-conflict view); here encoded as the version-delta view. Gold = Ver (framework API version) + Res (interface availability).

Hardware components 'use old API' after a ros2_control update: the framework's hardware-interface API version changed, so components compiled against the old API no longer load. Modeled UPGRADE targeting the framework API version (no message edge; the contract surface is the hardware_interface API, encoded as the changed signatures). consumer_reads = the SystemInterface API the component implements. Gold = Ver (targets framework API version). No pub/sub edge, so outputs/inputs empty.

Action client/server definition version mismatch: the action interface (goal/result/feedback) differs between client and server because their action definitions are at different versions, so the action handshake fails. Modeled UPGRADE on an action message edge with an interface-hash skew and a changed goal/result field. Action is encoded as a single msg_type role (the canonical schema has no action-triple field; the goal/result/feedback are captured in consumer_reads and changed_fields). Gold = Ver + Sig.
